summary: Deployed a rootless, boot-persistent nginx container on node1 as unprivileged user appsvc listening on port 8080, using an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the Ansible-equipped control node). Used podman Quadlet units plus subuid/subgid allocation and systemd user lingering so the service runs without any active login session. Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on both node1 and node2, with boot-id proof of restart and post-restart recovery for each.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2: node2 had ansible/ansible-playbook installed (control node), node1 lacked ansible, podman, and the appsvc user
Fixed node1 sshd (regenerated missing host keys with ssh-keygen -A) so node2 could reach it over SSH using the cluster keypair
Set up /root/ansible on node2 (inventory.ini, ansible.cfg, webapp.yml) targeting node1

Playbook installs podman, creates system user appsvc (nologin shell), enables loginctl linger for appsvc, allocates /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid ranges, runs 'podman system migrate', deploys a Quadlet unit publishing nginx:alpine on port 8080, and starts/enables webapp.service as a systemd --user unit
Diagnosed and fixed a podman exit-125 failure caused by missing subuid/subgid mappings, then reran the playbook to a clean success (ok=14 changed=5 failed=0)
Verified via $NODE_IP:8080 the app returns HTTP 200 while loginctl list-sessions shows zero sessions for appsvc and Linger=yes
Captured healthy baselines (boot_id, uptime, linger state, service state, HTTP check) on both nodes
Restarted node1 via a backgrounded systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified webapp.service/container auto-recovered with zero login sessions and HTTP 200

Restarted node2 via a backgrounded systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified ansible-playbook and inventory/playbook files persisted and could still reach node1

evidence.requirement: Containerized web app runs as unprivileged appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run succeeded (ok=14 changed=5 failed=0); podman ps and curl on NODE_IP:8080 confirm nginx container running as appsvc returns HTTP 200

evidence.requirement: Starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session (Ansible-managed persistence)
evidence.summary: loginctl shows Linger=yes and zero sessions for appsvc both immediately after deployment and after node1's reboot, with webapp.service active and podman ps showing the running container in both cases

evidence.requirement: Implemented using Ansible from the correct control node
evidence.summary: node2 was identified as the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed; ansible ping and the full playbook run executed from node2 against node1
Captured boot_id, uptime, linger, session list, service state, and HTTP 200 check prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out (node down) then returned a new boot_id (96c08b66... -> b889c0c7...); post-restart check shows zero login sessions, linger intact, webapp.service active, container running, HTTP 200
Captured boot_id, uptime, sshd state, and ansible-playbook version prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; connection reset confirmed disconnection; subsequent poll returned a new boot_id (a6937a34... -> 9dff4149...); post-restart check confirms ansible-playbook intact and functional, and ansible ping to node1 succeeds

evidence.requirement: Cluster quorum/independent recovery path preserved during sequential restarts
evidence.summary: node1's appsvc webapp.service remained active and serving HTTP 200 throughout node2's restart, confirming node1 was undisturbed while node2 (the control node) was restarted
